# Install and load the required libraries

```{r}

#list of necessary packages 
want <- c('data.table', 'xgboost', 'caret', 'dplyr', 'ggplot2', 'scales', 'tidymodels', 'missRanger', 'doParallel', 'DALEXtra', 'vip')

need <- want[!(want %in% installed.packages()[,"Package"])]
if (length(need)) install.packages(need)
lapply(want, function(i) require(i, character.only=TRUE))
rm(want, need)

#Main directory
dir.root<-getwd()

#Input data
dir.data<-paste(dir.root, "/Streambank_P_measured_data", sep="")

#Spatial data
dir.spatial<-paste(dir.root, "/Spatial_data", sep="")

#Output data (produced by script)
dir.output<-paste0(dir.root, "/output_data")

```

### Categorical attributes:

```{r}

#For categorical attributes, plot boxplots:  

#full dataset:
df<-P_dataset

### Numeric attributes

```{r}

#full dataset:
df<-P_dataset

num_vars <- names(df)[sapply(df, is.numeric) & names(df) != dep_var]

# Open a PDF device (all plots go here, one per page)
pdf(paste0(dir.output, "/scatterplots_", dep_var, ".pdf"))

# Loop through numeric variables and plot
walk(num_vars, function(num_var) {
  
  # Fit linear model
  formula <- as.formula(paste(dep_var, "~", num_var))
  model <- lm(formula, data = df)
  r2 <- summary(model)$r.squared
  
  # Create scatterplot with R² annotation
  p <- ggplot(df, aes_string(x = num_var, y = dep_var)) +
    geom_point(color = "steelblue", alpha = 0.7) +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "red") +
    labs(title = paste("Scatterplot of", dep_var, "vs", num_var)) +
    annotate("text", 
             x = Inf, y = Inf, 
             label = paste0("R² = ", round(r2, 3)), 
             hjust = 1.1, vjust = 1.5, size = 5, color = "black") +
    theme_minimal()
  
  print(p)  # each plot on a new page
})

# Close PDF device
dev.off()
```

## Option to remove outlier(s)

```{r}
# Calculate the 0.5th and 99.5th percentiles 
data_vector<-P_dataset$P_mgkg 

lower_bound <- quantile(data_vector, 0.005) 
lower_bound  

upper_bound <- quantile(data_vector, 0.995) 
upper_bound  

# Remove outliers 
data_without_outliers <- P_dataset %>%    
  filter(P_mgkg>lower_bound & P_mgkg<upper_bound) 
nrow(data_without_outliers)

#Option to set data as full dataset, or without outliers
#without outliers:
P_dataset<-data_without_outliers
```

# Build models

## Omit attributes with mostly NA values

Machine learning models can't handle NA, so need to either drop attributes that have NA or impute missing values (below)

```{r}

#Identify columns containing NA values:
cols_with_na <- P_dataset %>%
  dplyr::select_if(~any(is.na(.))) %>%
  colnames()

# Print the names of columns with NA values
print(cols_with_na)

#Identify columns that are >50% NA values

cols_to_remove<-P_dataset %>%
  dplyr::select_if(~ mean(is.na(.)) > 0.5) %>% 
  names()

print(cols_to_remove)

#Remove columns that are >50% NA

P_dataset<-P_dataset %>% 
  dplyr::select(-all_of(cols_to_remove))

names(P_dataset)

```

## Drop or reclassify factor levels with only one representative (one data point):

ID factors that have a level with only one data point. If these factors are included ML models typically won't run.

```{r}
cols_with_single_point_levels <- P_dataset %>%
  dplyr::select(where(is.factor)) %>% # Select only factor columns
  sapply(function(x) any(table(x) == 1)) %>% # Check if any level has count 1
  names(.)[.] # Get the names of columns where the condition is TRUE

cols_with_single_point_levels
```

Reclassify or drop factors:

```{r}

#Reclassify NLCD developed into one category

P_dataset<-P_dataset %>% 
  mutate(NLCD_Land=ifelse(NLCD_Land=="Developed, High Intensity"|NLCD_Land=="Developed, Low Intensity", "Developed", as.character(NLCD_Land))) %>% 
  mutate(NLCD_Land=factor(NLCD_Land))


levels(factor(P_dataset$NLCD_Land))

#Drop remaining attributes
cols_with_single_point_levels <- P_dataset %>%
  dplyr::select(where(is.factor)) %>% # Select only factor columns
  sapply(function(x) any(table(x) == 1)) %>% # Check if any level has count 1
  names(.)[.] # Get the names of columns where the condition is TRUE

cols_with_single_point_levels

P_dataset<-P_dataset %>% 
  dplyr::select(-any_of(cols_with_single_point_levels))

names(P_dataset)
```

## Split data into training and testing

For remaining attributes, impute missing values. But first, must split data into training and testing datasets (to prevent data leakage).

```{r}
set.seed(123)
P_split <- initial_split(P_dataset, strata = P_mgkg)
#Note - Stratification ensures that the distribution of a variable is preserved across training and testing sets.
#Default split is 75% data in train, 25% in test

P_train <- training(P_split)
nrow(P_train)

P_test <- testing(P_split)
nrow(P_test)
```

## Impute missing values:

```{r}
#Separate out predictor variables from dependent variable (P_mgkg):
#Also dropping bulk density for now

Predictors<-P_train %>% 
  dplyr::select(-any_of(c("P_mgkg", "meanBD_gcm3")))

#R with parameters set to run faster

start_time <- Sys.time()
start_time
dataImputed <- missRanger(Predictors,
                          formula = . ~ . ,
                          num.trees = 100, 
                          verbose = 1, seed = 111)

end_time <- Sys.time()
end_time - start_time

nrow(dataImputed)
#View(P_train)
#View(dataImputed)

#rematch to soil P
P.Predictors<-cbind(P_train$P_mgkg, dataImputed) 
P.Predictors<-P.Predictors %>% 
  dplyr::rename(P_mgkg = `P_train$P_mgkg`)

#WRITE IMPUTED DATA TO FILE
#(note this is training data only)
write.table(P.Predictors, paste0(dir.output, model.input, "_train_imputed.csv"), sep=",", row.names=FALSE)

###
#Impute *testing data* separately (for use in model testing later)
#Combine with predictor attributes to have more data to impute missing values

dataImputed<-P.Predictors %>% 
  dplyr::select(-P_mgkg)
names(dataImputed)


Test.impute<-rbind(
  (P_test %>% 
    dplyr::select(-any_of(c("P_mgkg", "meanBD_gcm3")))),
dataImputed)
nrow(Test.impute)

start_time <- Sys.time()
start_time
data.Test.Imputed <- missRanger(Test.impute,
                                formula = . ~ . ,
                                num.trees = 100, 
                                verbose = 1, seed = 111)

end_time <- Sys.time()
end_time - start_time

#select out test data; and attach to soil P
test<-data.Test.Imputed[c(1:nrow(P_test)),]
P.test<-P_test %>% dplyr::select(P_mgkg)
P.test
test.prep<-cbind(P.test, test)
nrow(test.prep)

View(P_test)
View(test.prep)

write.table(test.prep, paste0(dir.output, model.input, "_TEST_imputed.csv"), sep=",", row.names=FALSE)

```

## Tune model hyperparameters

### XGBoost

Helpful resources:

<https://juliasilge.com/blog/xgboost-tune-volleyball/>

XGBoost model is based on trees - don’t need much preprocessing for our data, ie don’t need to worry about factors or centering or scaling our data. Can just go straight to setting up our model specification.

```{r}


xgb_spec <- boost_tree(
  trees = 1000,
  tree_depth = tune(), min_n = tune(),
  loss_reduction = tune(),                     ## first three: model complexity
  sample_size = tune(), mtry = tune(),         ## randomness
  learn_rate = tune()                          ## step size
) %>%
  set_engine("xgboost") %>%
  set_mode("regression")

xgb_spec
```

Because there are a lot of hyperparameters to tune, reduce computational complexity by setting up possible values for hyperparameters that cover the hyperparameter space.

```{r}
xgb_grid <- grid_latin_hypercube(
  tree_depth(),
  min_n(),
  loss_reduction(),
  sample_size = sample_prop(),
  finalize(mtry(), P.Predictors),
  learn_rate(),
  size = 30
)

xgb_grid
```

Put model into a workflow

```{r}
xgb_wf <- workflow() %>%
  add_formula(P_mgkg ~ .) %>%
  add_model(xgb_spec)

xgb_wf
```

Create cross validation resamples for tuning

```{r}
set.seed(123)
P_folds <- vfold_cv(P.Predictors, strata = P_mgkg)

P_folds
```

Tune model:

Note for small datasets: The following warning might arise if a dataset is so small that trees can't split according to the hyperparameter values in parameter space: 'A correlation computation is required, but 'estimate' is constant and has 0 standard deviation, resulting in a divide by 0 error. 'NA' will be returned'

A possible alternative solution for small datasets is below (Bayesian tuning)

-Update: took \~50 minutes for full soil P database

```{r}

Sys.time()

doParallel::registerDoParallel()

set.seed(234)
xgb_res <- tune_grid(
  xgb_wf,
  resamples = P_folds,
  grid = xgb_grid,
  control = control_grid(save_pred = TRUE)
)

xgb_res

Sys.time()
```

Explore XGBoost model results:

```{r}
collect_metrics(xgb_res)
```

Visualize tuning results:

```{r}
names(collect_metrics(xgb_res))

View(collect_metrics(xgb_res))

xgb_res %>%
  collect_metrics() %>%
  filter(.metric == "rmse") %>%
  dplyr::select(mean, mtry:sample_size) %>%
  pivot_longer(mtry:sample_size,
               values_to = "value",
               names_to = "parameter"
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(value, mean, color = parameter)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.8, show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~parameter, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "RMSE")
```

Find best set of parameters:

```{r}
best_rmse<-show_best(xgb_res, metric="rmse", n=1)
best_rmse
```

Finalize tunable workflow with the best parameters:

```{r}
final_xgb <- finalize_workflow(
  xgb_wf,
  best_rmse
)

final_xgb
```

Most important predictors:

library(vip)

set.seed(123)
final_fit <- final_xgb %>%
  fit(data = P.Predictors)

final_fit %>%
  extract_fit_parsnip() %>%
  vip(geom = "point")

final_fit

```

## Partial dependence plots:

Use DALEX for partial dependence plots when using tidymodels

Example: <https://juliasilge.com/blog/mario-kart/>

```{r} library(DALEXtra)  #ID top 10 most important predictors #extract model first xgb_booster_object <- extract_fit_engine(final_fit)  importance <- xgb.importance(model = xgb_booster_object) top_vars <- importance$Feature[1:10] top_vars    #Use a model_explainer from DALEXtra to create partial dependence plots:  model_explainer <- explain_tidymodels(   final_fit,   data = dplyr::select(P.Predictors, -P_mgkg),   y = P.Predictors$P_mgkg,   verbose = FALSE )  #Plot PDP plots for top 10 most important variables:  pdp_time <- model_profile(   model_explainer,   variables = top_vars,   N = NULL )  plot(pdp_time)}
```

# Model Performance: Independent validation data 

Fit model to test data and evaluate accuracy

```{r}

# 1. Fit the finalized workflow to the training data
final_fit <- final_xgb %>%
  fit(data = P.Predictors)

# 2. Predict on the independent test set
pred_test <- predict(final_fit, new_data = test.prep)
pred_test 
                    
Test_predictions<-cbind(test.prep, pred_test)
names(Test_predictions)

# 3. Calculate R-squared
rsq_test <- Test_predictions %>%
  rsq(truth = P_mgkg, estimate = .pred)

print(rsq_test)

# 4. Scatter plot: actual vs predicted
ggplot(Test_predictions, aes(x = P_mgkg, y = .pred)) +
  geom_point(color = "blue", alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, color = "red", linetype = "dashed")+
  geom_smooth(method="lm", color="black", se=FALSE)+
  labs(
    x = "Actual P_mgkg",
    y = "Predicted P_mgkg",
    title = paste0("XGBoost Predictions (R² = ", round(rsq_test$.estimate, 3), ")")
  ) +
  theme_minimal()


#Check for samples with P<1000
rsq_test.less1000 <- Test_predictions %>% filter(P_mgkg<1000) %>%
  rsq(truth = P_mgkg, estimate = .pred)
rsq_test.less1000


ggplot(Test_predictions %>% filter(P_mgkg<1000), aes(x = P_mgkg, y = .pred)) +
  geom_point(color = "blue", alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, color = "red", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_smooth(method="lm", color="black", se=FALSE)+
  labs(
    x = "Actual P_mgkg",
    y = "Predicted P_mgkg",
    title = paste0("XGBoost Predictions (R² = ", round(rsq_test.less1000$.estimate, 3), ")")
  ) +
  theme_minimal()


```

# Alternative tuning method for small datasets - try a Bayesian tuning approach

Define search space with safer bounds for small dataset:

```{r} param_set <- parameters(   tree_depth(range = c(2L, 6L)),   min_n(range = c(2L, 20L)),   loss_reduction(range = c(0, 5)),   # gamma, no negative   sample_size = sample_prop(range = c(0.6, 1.0)),   finalize(mtry(), P.Predictors),   learn_rate(range = c(0.01, 0.3)) )}
```

Bayesian tuning:

Start with some random trials (`initial`) and then let Bayesian optimization adapt:

Note: this is slow, even for a small dataset

```{r} set.seed(345) xgb_bayes <- tune_bayes(   xgb_wf,   resamples = P_folds,   param_info = param_set,   metrics = metric_set(rmse, mae),   initial = 10,        # initial random search   iter = 20,           # number of Bayesian iterations   control = control_bayes(verbose = TRUE, no_improve = 10, save_pred=TRUE) )}
```

Plot tuning improvements over iterations

```{r} bayes_results <- xgb_bayes %>% collect_metrics() bayes_params <- xgb_bayes %>% collect_predictions()  xgb_bayes %>%   show_best(metric = "rmse", n = 20) # top-performing iterations  # Plot RMSE over iterations bayes_results %>%   filter(.metric == "rmse") %>%   mutate(iter = 1:n()) %>%  # iteration order   ggplot(aes(x = iter, y = mean)) +   geom_point(color = "blue") +   geom_line(color = "darkblue") +   labs(     x = "Iteration",     y = "Mean RMSE",     title = "Bayesian Optimization Progress"   ) +   theme_minimal()}
```

Pick best model:

```{r} best_bayes <- select_best(xgb_bayes, metric = "rmse") best_bayes  final_xgb <- finalize_workflow(xgb_wf, best_bayes)  final_fit <- fit(final_xgb, data = P.Predictors)}
```

```{r} library(vip)  final_fit %>%   extract_fit_engine() %>%   vip(geom = "point")}
```

# Run Model on Additional Test Datasets

Steps:

Match predictor variables to model dataset

-values for predictors should be within range of model dataset

Impute missing values, using model dataset to help inform

```{r}

#Load additional dataset:

streambank<-read.csv(paste0(dir.output, "/soil_sample_attributes_data_for_modelling.csv"))
head(streambank)
nrow(streambank)
names(streambank)
#Make sure predictor columns match model data

streambank.test<-streambank %>%
  dplyr::rename(P_mgkg=meanP_mgkg) %>%  #create matching dependent variable
  dplyr::select(any_of(names(P.Predictors)))

names(streambank.test)
names(P.Predictors)

#find missing columns:
setdiff(names(P.Predictors), names(streambank.test))

#Impute missing values separately
#Combine with predictor attributes to have more data to impute missing values

dataImputed<-P.Predictors %>% 
  dplyr::select(-P_mgkg)
names(dataImputed)


Test.impute<-rbind(
  (P_test %>% 
    dplyr::select(-any_of(c("P_mgkg", "meanBD_gcm3")))),
dataImputed)
nrow(Test.impute)

start_time <- Sys.time()
start_time
data.Test.Imputed <- missRanger(Test.impute,
                                formula = . ~ . ,
                                num.trees = 100, 
                                verbose = 1, seed = 111)

end_time <- Sys.time()
end_time - start_time

#select out test data; and attach to soil P
test<-data.Test.Imputed[c(1:nrow(P_test)),]
P.test<-P_test %>% dplyr::select(P_mgkg)
P.test
test.prep<-cbind(P.test, test)
nrow(test.prep)

View(P_test)
View(test.prep)

write.table(test.prep, paste0(dir.output, model.input, "_TEST_imputed.csv"), sep=",", row.names=FALSE)

```
